obligation: E-ISAC notice of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident (low impact)
trigger: A Cyber Security Incident that compromised or disrupted a low impact BES Cyber System at Substation N or Substation E (NERC Glossary definition of Reportable Cyber Security Incident)
deadline: CIP-003-9 sets no fixed time; it requires the determination and then notification unless prohibited by law. Company target: within 1 hour of the determination (POL-03 4.4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - low impact BES Cyber Systems at 2 substations

obligation: CIP-008-6 R4 Reportable Cyber Security Incident notification
trigger: Reportable incident or attempt to compromise involving high or medium impact BES Cyber Systems or their EACMS
deadline: Within 1 hour after determination of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident; by end of next calendar day for an attempt to compromise; updates within 7 calendar days of new information
applies_at_this_tier: No - CIP-008-6 Table R4 applies only to high and medium impact systems; the company has low impact only (P03 G-042)

citation: Form DOE-417 criteria 2 and 3; Federal Energy Administration Act of 1974 sec. 13(b) (Pub. L. 93-275); OMB 1901-0288
trigger: Criterion 2: a Reportable Cyber Security Incident. Criterion 3: a cyber event that is not a Reportable Cyber Security Incident but causes interruptions of electrical system operations (for example, unauthorized SCADA commands that open feeders)
deadline: Within 1 hour of the incident (telephone notice to the DOE Operations Center is acceptable when operations are critical, followed by the written form)
notify: DOE (DOE-417 online system; DOE Operations Center by phone as backup). The form lets the filer choose to share it with NERC, the E-ISAC, and CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - electric utility. Give the Balancing Authority the information it needs and file directly unless the BA files for the company (agree in advance; P03 G-051)

trigger: Criterion 11: a cyber event that could potentially impact electric power system adequacy or reliability. Criterion 12: loss of electric service to more than 50,000 customers for 1 hour or more (and no Emergency Alert criterion applies)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 72,000 meters, so a wide outage can meet criterion 12

citation: Form DOE-417 instructions (Update Report; Final Report)
trigger: Significant new information after an Emergency Alert or Normal Report; every filed report
deadline: Update when significant information becomes available; final report (updated Schedule 1 and all of Schedule 2) within 72 hours of the incident unless an interim update has been provided

citation: NERC EOP-004-4 R2 and Attachment 1 (Distribution Provider events)
trigger: Damage or destruction of a company Facility from actual or suspected intentional human action; physical threat or suspicious device or activity at a Facility; uncontrolled loss of 200 MW or more of firm load for 15 minutes or more
deadline: By the later of 24 hours after recognizing the event met a threshold or the end of the next business day (4 p.m. local time)
notify: NERC (systemawareness@nerc.net) and the parties in the Operating Plan (Reliability Coordinator; law enforcement where relevant). A DOE-417 form may be used as the report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - DP is a listed entity. A pure cyber intrusion is not an Attachment 1 event unless it causes one of these outcomes

obligation: Operational notice to the transmission owner, Balancing Authority, and Reliability Coordinator
trigger: Any event that affects 115 kV protection at Substation N or E, or load served from the BES
deadline: Immediately by phone from the DCC
notify: Transmission owner control center; BA; RC
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and operational, not a cyber reporting rule

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents: for example, name with SSN (held in the CIS), or portal user name with password. OMS names, addresses, and phone numbers are not listed data elements; counsel decides whether OMS premise map locations count as geolocation information under 501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VII)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Only if CIS or other personal information is accessed; not expected in an OT-only intrusion

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Florida residents are affected

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
applies_at_this_tier: Only if more than 1,000 individuals are notified

obligation: Vendor breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (for example, the CIS vendor) discovers a breach of the company's customer personal information
deadline: Within 10 days after determination; contracts should require faster notice (POL-01 4.9)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in the CIS and AMI contracts

trigger: Affected customers who reside outside Florida (for example, seasonal residents with an out-of-state address)
notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residence of affected customers

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
trigger: Considering any payment to an extortionist
deadline: Before any payment; reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
deadline: As soon as practicable (company target: same day)
notify: CISA (report.cisa.gov or CISA Central); FBI field office
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary; supports response help and OFAC mitigation

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's hotline before hiring response vendors)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25. If finalized as proposed, the company would be covered regardless of size under proposed 226.2(b)(6), because it must file DOE-417 and report under the NERC CIP standards

trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a TSA-designated pipeline
deadline: No later than 72 hours after identification
notify: CISA Central; CISA shares with TSA
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company operates no pipelines

trigger: Cyber attack on a power reactor licensee's digital assets
deadline: 1 hour / 4 hours / 8 hours depending on event
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no NRC reactor license
